observations: case_axi_ddr_interface is the direct executed current-layer failure. Its blockers are identity binding, Vivado-export compile authority, ordered-command authority references, and simulator executable authorization; the current functional precondition additionally lacks exact_sample_top_module loading.

functional_sim=fail is dependency-blocked because case_vcs_functional_sim was skipped behind case_axi_ddr_interface. Missing board_axi_ddr semantic evidence and missing runtime reports are downstream absence cascades, not independently localized hardware failures.

The CCTG/debug closure records verification_capability_gap, no failed causal boundary, no root candidate module, and no lower-layer evidence challenge. Therefore a board trace is required only after the verification capability is restored.

Live hash-validated operator-leaf and connected single-transformer-layer certificates remain reusable. The connected kernel is certified as an elastic variable-latency token pipeline with ordered boundaries and required cross-token overlap; unequal same-token stage timing is not a failure. No current trace contradicts either certificate.

Prior repair feedback about remote_tool_failure is historical-only for hardware diagnosis, but it establishes a current framework capability gap: the runner/analyzer must distinguish normal completion, simulator fatal, external signal/kill, and timeout with raw terminal provenance before a future replay may be interpreted as a DUT liveness failure.

sacg_memory_truth reports 15 active scoped contamination barriers and six open scoped retry requests. The rejected Stage7 and Stage8 artifacts are planning/debug inputs only; they cannot be promoted or consumed as validated board evidence. The older barrier signatures do not override the supplied current gate status or establish a new RTL root cause.
No conditional specialist was triggered: design_team status is no_split. The repair decision remains constrained by the direct tool evidence and current-layer hierarchy policy.
proposed_actions: Repair only the generated board-simulation loader/harness binding and canonical compile-plan metadata against the already discovered exact sample-project identity; preserve wrapper and semantic contract hashes.
Implement the missing remote VCS termination-provenance capture and checker, then replay the unchanged hash-bound board closure with boundary instrumentation.
If the replay exposes a real simulator/DUT failure, create a CCTG causal slice before any code repair; only an explicit named lower-layer contradiction may trigger targeted lower-layer revalidation.
If the replay passes, rerun the remaining affected board-layer gate DAG, assemble semantic evidence, and reconcile SACG only after every required current-layer gate passes.
risks: Changing or fabricating board top-module names, simulator executables, Vivado contexts, wrapper sources, or compile commands would invalidate exact sample-project identity rather than repair it. The repair must derive all values from current discovery and export facts.

A telemetry-only remote runner change must not alter checkpoint, stimulus, reference output, numeric policy, tolerance, testbench semantic contract, wrapper source hashes, compilation source set, or simulation behavior. It must only expose termination provenance.

A successful VCS compile or independent AXI/prefetch progress is not a board functional, lifecycle, output-frontier, liveness, or semantic pass. Terminal completion and target-model output comparison remain required.

The next board replay must bind a complete Transformer-block checkpoint tensor catalog, deterministic or real stimulus provenance, independent target-model Transformer-block expected outputs, immutable numeric comparison policy, generated semantic-testbench hashes, and executed complete-scope DUT weight-consumption evidence. Embedding/tokenization, final norm, LM head/logits, and sampling remain outside DUT scope.

If a replay reports a real value, order, protocol, or liveness failure, patching an output-side module or reopening lower layers without earliest-boundary localization would violate the hierarchical repair loop. A lower-layer backtrack additionally requires direct current core-start, ingress, egress, causal-boundary, and named-certificate contradiction evidence.
Until the complete Stage7 DAG passes and SACG retry/barrier reconciliation succeeds, synthesis, implementation, bitstream generation, runtime-ABI release, and board runtime remain blocked.
